source.title: IMS Bearing Data Set
source.publisher: NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence Data Set Repository
source.license: NASA Open Data marks access as public and links the USA.gov government-works notice; original provider is IMS, University of Cincinnati
source.acquisition: Three test-to-failure experiments; four bearings per shaft at 2,000 RPM and 6,000 lb radial load; 20 kHz one-second snapshots; eight accelerometer channels in set 1 and four in sets 2 and 3; documented natural end-state failures in four bearing installations.
source.use: Natural run-to-failure, multi-bearing, multi-sensor external fail-closed boundary evaluation only; never production training.

selection: Seven linearly spaced, timestamp-ordered snapshots from each official experiment interval, fixed before inference; every sensor channel in every selected snapshot is evaluated.
transform: No resampling, synthesis, relabeling, or amplitude transform; original 20,480-point ASCII channels at 20 kHz and documented 2,000 RPM.
claim: Natural run-to-failure, multi-bearing, multi-sensor fail-closed boundary probe; not a natural-fault sensitivity estimate, early-warning claim, or field pilot.
limitations: The NASA/IMS experiments are accelerated laboratory run-to-failure histories, not a prospective industrial field pilot.
RotorNote was not trained on IMS and all cases are outside its fitted RPM/training envelope; this receipt proves abstention behavior only.
Seven predeclared timestamps per experiment test early, intermediate, and documented endpoint behavior but do not estimate natural-fault sensitivity or warning lead time.
